title: Same-glyph ink gaps support graded separators in sampled quires
statement: Measure two differently labelled separators between the same ordered glyph pair on the same Yale scan line. Readers locate the strokes from a separator-erased glyph sequence and mark the ink extrema before the labels are revealed. Compare this physical audit with an exact-pair reanalysis of a much larger published ink-gap table.
check: Repeat the frozen matched-line sampler, recover the same whole-line crops from the Yale IIIF manifest, and give randomized unlabeled crop panels to additional readers. Extend whole-line segmentation to the unsupported layouts. Compare the signed within-line width difference across quires with the least reliable lines retained as unresolved, and measure how often alternative alignments reverse the effect.

sources.primary: Liudmila Rozanova and Alexander Temerev (2026), A Glyph Is Not a Letter, a Token Is Not a Word, a Space Is Not a Space, section 2.6 and Appendix A.3. https://arxiv.org/html/2608.17096v1#A1.SS3
sources.native_scans: Yale Beinecke MS 408, https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/2002046. Native region request uses the canvas numeric ID and the same reported x0 and y0 origin.
sources.s45_line_detection: Jonathan Simone, S45 data, archived commit 713fa1003dd56e9526e8596f57128e60e18c02d6. https://github.com/thisisntjon/voynich/tree/713fa1003dd56e9526e8596f57128e60e18c02d6/record/runs/s45
sources.s47_measurements: Jonathan Simone, F-19/S47, https://simoneresearch.com/research/voynich/atlas/f-19/ and https://github.com/thisisntjon/voynich/tree/713fa1003dd56e9526e8596f57128e60e18c02d6/record/runs/s47. positions.tsv SHA256 8284089a44b7a8da4240eb7b9c951f676a6906a3867dd67be789d73d694a6a19.
sources.alternate_line_registration: Voynichese archive word-coordinate data, used in this audit only as guides to the intended whole lines on alternate layouts. https://github.com/lrozanova/voynich-units/tree/main/data/voynich-units/morphometry_voynichese/voynichese_boxes

prior_evidence: Rozanova and Temerev found a strong distinction using Voynichese token boxes. Their direct pixel pilot measures the physical ink but uses those same boxes to locate gaps on six folios. It retains 265 certain and 21 uncertain gaps, giving a mean contrast of +1.84 pixels at 700 pixels page width. Its eighteen exact-pair comparisons were post hoc. The present spot audit matches both glyphs on the same line prospectively and gives the readers no inherited word boxes.

primary_method.sampling: Use the public practice training set. Retain paragraph lines composed entirely of lowercase EVA and literal comma or period after deleting edge paragraph markers. In EVA-basic select a period and a comma on the same line with exactly the same ordered glyph pair. The frozen 27 cases use distinct numbered leaves. Twelve quires contribute two cases of at most two separator ordinals apart and three additional eligible quires contribute one case with a cap of two or four ordinals. Optimize opposite left-to-right label orientations, then ordinal distance and exact pair diversity, with SHA256-seeded tie breaks. The original selection had 16 period-left and 11 period-right cases.
primary_method.whole_line_localization: Use only the S45 image-native baselines and polygons from unique 1:1 row matches, giving 18 lines from ten quires. The existing whole-line correspondence uses continuous glyph counts, without specifying where either sampled separator lies. Exclude seven compound or foldout loci that lack the corresponding S45 crop, and two loci with non-1:1 matches. Native photographs are displayed as padded whole-line strips, retaining useful context for ambiguous tall strokes. There are no imported boundaries or word boxes on the displayed ink.
primary_method.blinding: Four auxiliary image-model readers independently inspect overlapping groups of anonymous strips, so two readers cover each initial line. Each panel has a native pixel ruler and a detached reference in EVA-basic with every separator removed. Two randomized A and B markers in that reference indicate which stroke transitions to locate, without identifying their separator classes. The reference x positions are unrelated to the photograph. Give readers no physical word locations or separator categories. The panel ordering and marker labels use seed 104081551.
primary_method.measurement: Each reader matches the full unspaced sequence by inspection, then records the left glyph's rightmost horizontal ink extent and the right glyph's leftmost extent. Use max(0,right-left-1) native pixels so touching or overlapping glyph envelopes contribute zero. Compare the same-line difference after averaging the two estimates and multiplying by 700 divided by native canvas width. Require all four estimated endpoints to agree between readers within 20 pixels; show a 10-pixel sensitivity. Quire means receive equal weight. Repeat the quire-cluster bootstrap 4,000 times with fixed seed 20261126. This is a small convenience sample among eligible lines with measurable geometry, and the intervals are descriptive.
primary_method.companion_checks: The archive's initial folios are f7v, f14v, f23r, f39v, f42v and f56v. Repeat the primary result after excluding them. Independently try one wider crop for the clipped right edge and one additional reader for an exact repeated-glyph alignment disagreement. Keep these recovery measurements outside the primary tally. A further alternative-layout check uses whole-line locators cross-registered with old archive boxes and normal-light Yale crops, without giving the optical readers either target coordinates or separator classes. The whole-canvas width conversion compresses units differently on wide foldouts, so use native edges and the within-line sign for the supplemental comparison.

s47_reanalysis_method.mapping: Read the published S47 positions on public scans. Read the pinned raw ZL paragraph lines using the strict clean-line rule. Reconstruct the entire ordinal sequence of periods, commas and internal positions with the S47 glyph segmentation (EVA-basic plus iiin, iin, in, iir, ir and ee). Require exact agreement to the observed row labels and lengths before transferring any glyph-pair identities. Drop lines with any missing width; use the nearest same-pair cross-class match per line, breaking ties by period ordinal, then comma ordinal. This additional filter avoids choosing gaps by magnitude.
s47_reanalysis_method.comparison: Subtract uncertain width from certain width and divide by the published geometric threshold for that line. Report both pooled results and equally weighted quire means. Recompute descriptive percentile intervals with 4,000 quire resamples and seed 1947. Check orientation, proximity, quire exclusion and the alignment branches with equal or unequal detected versus transcribed token counts. The published table has 2,441 loci with emitted positions, including width-gate failures.
s47_reanalysis_method.independence_limit: S47 ink segmentation precedes transcription alignment, but its width at a separator depends on alignment to transcribed tokens. Some within-token distances are placed at proportional glyph offsets. Guarding on exact ordinal sequence and exact glyph pair leaves this dependency in place. The larger reanalysis tests robustness of the archived measurements and the small blind audit tests independence of the pixel edges.

sampling_record.glyph_convention: EVA-basic token-internal segmentation. Glyphs are indexed from zero in the concatenated segmented words. Raw EVA character offsets also start at zero and mark a point between characters.
sampling_record.selection: Two different numbered leaves per A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,M,N,S,T; distance ≤2. Optimize opposite dot/comma orientations, then summed distance, then distinct edge pairs, then seeded SHA-256 order. Add one in each I,O,Q in that order at caps 4,2,4; minimize orientation imbalance then distance then seeded SHA-256 order. IDs sorted by the same seeded hash.

additional_blind_recovery.reason: Right-hand letter of B was outside original whole-line crop. Expand only right edge and preserve original x origin and sequence.
Third blinded reader aligns the B separator between the two consecutive tedy groups. The original discrepant read placed that target at the earlier chety–tedy junction. No image replacement.

interpretation: Both masked readers matched all four edges within 20 native pixels for 14 of the 18 initial crops, spanning ten quires. The certain gap is larger in each measured pair. The equal-quire contrast is +3.75 pixels rescaled to a 700-pixel page. Excluding pages from the original direct ink study leaves 12 of 12 positive cases with an equal-quire contrast of +3.42 pixels. Both left-to-right label orientations give the same direction.

The exception log is part of the result. Two initially mapped photographs do not provide reliable matches to the complete reference row. One crop cuts off the right glyph and one repeated sequence received discrepant placements. Expanded-crop recovery and a tie-breaking reader are reported separately. The alternate locators broaden coverage across compound leaves while keeping the sample small and conditional on visually identifiable glyphs.

All 25 resolved comparisons were wider at the period across 15 marked quire groups. This combines the primary sample, nine supplemental whole-line matches and two recoveries. Only the explicitly specified 14 are used for the primary width estimate.

In the larger archived-pixel analysis, 99 of 121 exact-pair lines on 54 pages or panels favor the certain gap. The equal-quire mean difference is +0.269 threshold units with bootstrap interval [−0.757, +0.892]. An anomalous 242 px comma width at f35r.8 dominates one quire estimate, and our blind strip cannot safely verify the corresponding row. Equal-token-count cases alone have an equal-quire mean of −0.090, showing the dependence of the archive result on how its alignment branches contribute.

This documents the predicted physical spacing contrast in the identifiable same-glyph sample. The proportions cannot estimate the distribution of all spaces or establish the lexical status of either separator. Broad independent confirmation would require a larger set of reliably aligned image lines, especially at dense, interrupted, or heavily illustrated layouts.
